references.text: Prohibition against charging interest to poor Israelites who borrow money, a parallel command that expands on the ban against usury
Expanded legislation about helping poor brothers without charging interest or profiting from their distress
Nehemiah rebukes the people for charging interest to their brothers, a practical application of this commandment
The righteous person does not lend money at interest, a wisdom reflection on this commandment
A righteous man does not take interest or usury, a prophetic confirmation of the ban on interest
Whoever takes interest and usury shall die for their sin, a serious warning against breaking this commandment
The righteous son does not take interest, in contrast to his sinful father
Accusation against Jerusalem for taking interest and usury from their neighbors
Jesus teaches about lending without expecting anything back, an expansion of the principle of generous lending
